--src: Mathlib.Algebra.Module.Submodule.LinearMap
@[simp, norm_cast]
theorem coeFn_sum {ι : Type*} (t : Finset ι) (f : ι → M →ₛₗ[σ₁₂] M₂) :
    ⇑(∑ i ∈ t, f i) = ∑ i ∈ t, (f i : M → M₂) :=
  _root_.map_sum
    (show AddMonoidHom (M →ₛₗ[σ₁₂] M₂) (M → M₂)
      from { toFun := DFunLike.coe,
             map_zero' := rfl
             map_add' := fun _ _ => rfl }) _ _

--src: Mathlib.RingTheory.Ideal.Quotient.Basic
/-- If `f : R^n → R^m` is an `R`-linear map and `I ⊆ R` is an ideal, then the image of `I^n` is
    contained in `I^m`. -/
theorem map_pi {ι : Type*} [Finite ι] {ι' : Type w} (x : ι → R) (hi : ∀ i, x i ∈ I)
    (f : (ι → R) →ₗ[R] ι' → R) (i : ι') : f x i ∈ I := by
  classical
    cases nonempty_fintype ι
    rw [pi_eq_sum_univ x]
    simp only [Finset.sum_apply, smul_eq_mul, map_sum, Pi.smul_apply, map_smul]
    exact I.sum_mem fun j _ => I.mul_mem_right _ (hi j)

--src: Mathlib.RingTheory.Finiteness.Basic
instance pi {ι : Type*} {M : ι → Type*} [_root_.Finite ι] [∀ i, AddCommMonoid (M i)]
    [∀ i, Module R (M i)] [h : ∀ i, Module.Finite R (M i)] : Module.Finite R (∀ i, M i) :=
  ⟨by
    rw [← Submodule.pi_top]
    exact Submodule.fg_pi fun i => (h i).1⟩

--src: Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Pi
/-- The linear equivalence between linear functions on a finite product of modules and
families of functions on these modules. See note [bundled maps over different rings]. -/
@[simps symm_apply]
def lsum (S) [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M] [Fintype ι] [Semiring S] [Module S M]
    [SMulCommClass R S M] : ((i : ι) → φ i →ₗ[R] M) ≃ₗ[S] ((i : ι) → φ i) →ₗ[R] M where
  toFun f := ∑ i : ι, (f i).comp (proj i)
  invFun f i := f.comp (single R φ i)
  map_add' f g := by simp only [Pi.add_apply, add_comp, Finset.sum_add_distrib]
  map_smul' c f := by simp only [Pi.smul_apply, smul_comp, Finset.smul_sum, RingHom.id_apply]
  left_inv f := by
    ext i x
    simp [apply_single]
  right_inv f := by
    ext x
    suffices f (∑ j, Pi.single j (x j)) = f x by simpa [apply_single]
    rw [Finset.univ_sum_single]

--src: Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.Finprod
theorem finsum_mul {R : Type*} [Semiring R] (f : α → R) (r : R) (h : (support f).Finite) :
    (∑ᶠ a : α, f a) * r = ∑ᶠ a : α, f a * r :=
  (AddMonoidHom.mulRight r).map_finsum h

--src: Mathlib.RingTheory.MvPolynomial.WeightedHomogeneous
theorem DirectSum.coeLinearMap_eq_finsum [DecidableEq M]
    (x : DirectSum M fun i : M => ↥(weightedHomogeneousSubmodule R w i)) :
    (DirectSum.coeLinearMap fun i : M => weightedHomogeneousSubmodule R w i) x =
      finsum fun m => x m := by
  classical
  rw [DirectSum.coeLinearMap_eq_dfinsupp_sum, DFinsupp.sum, finsum_eq_sum_of_support_subset]
  apply DirectSum.support_subset

--src: Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.Finsupp
@[to_additive]
theorem prod_fintype [Fintype α] (f : α →₀ M) (g : α → M → N) (h : ∀ i, g i 0 = 1) :
    f.prod g = ∏ i, g i (f i) :=
  f.prod_of_support_subset (subset_univ _) g fun x _ => h x

--src: Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.TensorProduct.Vanishing
/-- Converse of `TensorProduct.vanishesTrivially_of_sum_tmul_eq_zero_of_rTensor_injective`.
Assume that every expression $\sum_i m_i \otimes n_i$ which vanishes also vanishes trivially.
Then, for every submodule $M' \subseteq M$, the map $M' \otimes N \to M \otimes N$ is injective. -/
theorem rTensor_injective_of_forall_vanishesTrivially
    (hMN : ∀ {ι : Type u} [Fintype ι] {m : ι → M} {n : ι → N},
      ∑ i, m i ⊗ₜ n i = (0 : M ⊗[R] N) → VanishesTrivially R m n)
    (M' : Submodule R M) : Injective (rTensor N M'.subtype) := by
  apply (injective_iff_map_eq_zero _).mpr
  rintro x hx
  obtain ⟨s, rfl⟩ := exists_finset x
  rw [← Finset.sum_attach]
  apply sum_tmul_eq_zero_of_vanishesTrivially
  simp only [map_sum, rTensor_tmul, coe_subtype] at hx
  have := hMN ((Finset.sum_attach s _).trans hx)
  unfold VanishesTrivially at this ⊢
  convert this with κ _ a y j
  symm
  convert (injective_iff_map_eq_zero' _).mp (injective_subtype M') _
  simp

--src: Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Finsupp.LSum
@[simp]
theorem sum_smul_index_linearMap' [Semiring R] [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M] [AddCommMonoid M₂]
    [Module R M₂] {v : α →₀ M} {c : R} {h : α → M →ₗ[R] M₂} :
    ((c • v).sum fun a => h a) = c • v.sum fun a => h a := by
  rw [Finsupp.sum_smul_index', Finsupp.smul_sum]
  · simp only [map_smul]
  · intro i
    exact (h i).map_zero

--src: Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Finsupp.Pi
theorem splittingOfFunOnFintypeSurjective_injective [Finite α] (f : M →ₗ[R] α → R)
    (s : Surjective f) : Injective (splittingOfFunOnFintypeSurjective f s) :=
  (leftInverse_splittingOfFunOnFintypeSurjective f s).injective

theorem LinearMap.finsum_apply {R : Type*} [Semiring R] {A B : Type*} [AddCommMonoid A] [Module R A]
    [AddCommMonoid B] [Module R B] {ι : Type*} [Finite ι] (φ : ∀ _ : ι, A →ₗ[R] B) (a : A) :
    (∑ᶠ i, φ i) a = ∑ᶠ i, φ i a := by
  induction ι using Finite.induction_empty_option
  · case of_equiv X Y e hx =>
    convert hx (φ ∘ e)
    · exact (finsum_comp_equiv e).symm
    · exact (finsum_comp_equiv e).symm
  · simp [finsum_of_isEmpty]
  · case h_option X _ hX =>
    rw [finsum_option (Set.toFinite _), finsum_option (Set.toFinite _)]
    simp [hX]

C1_dependencies.name: Finite.induction_empty_option
C1_dependencies.content:
/-- An induction principle for finite types, analogous to `Nat.rec`. It effectively says
that every `Fintype` is either `Empty` or `Option α`, up to an `Equiv`. -/
theorem Finite.induction_empty_option {P : Type u → Prop} (of_equiv : ∀ {α β}, α ≃ β → P α → P β)
    (h_empty : P PEmpty) (h_option : ∀ {α} [Fintype α], P α → P (Option α)) (α : Type u)
    [Finite α] : P α := by
  cases nonempty_fintype α
  refine Fintype.induction_empty_option ?_ ?_ ?_ α
  exacts [fun α β _ => of_equiv, h_empty, @h_option]
